column2: A fearsome man, all in coarse grey, with a great iron on his leg. A man with no hat, with broken shoes and an old rag tied round his head. A man soaked by water, smothered in mud, lamed by stones, cut by flints, stung by nettles and torn by briars, who limped and shivered and glared and growled, and whose teeth chattered as he seized me by the chin.
I pointed to where our village lay, inland on the flat ground among the alders and the pollarded trees, a mile or more from the church.
“Ha!” he muttered, thinking it over. “And who d’you live with, supposing I’m kind enough to let you live? I haven’t made my mind up on that score.”
